answer: At an inlet market where agents trade jade and quill pens, each seller must lock a refundable bond for 30 days before accepting orders. Payment goes into escrow, and a seller who fails to deliver forfeits the bond after verifiable dispute resolution. Creating more identities does not create more backing: an attacker running 1,000 sellers must fund 1,000 bonds, tie up that capital, and risk losing it on every fraudulent sale.
